title: Adiabatic Theory Data on Strongly Chirped Dissipative Solitons of the Cubic-Quintic Nonlinear Ginzburg-Landau Equation
authors: V. L. Kalashnikov, E. Sorokin, A. Rudenkov, I. T. Sorokina
abstract: This data article provides the datasets, symbolic derivations, and scripts used to reproduce master diagrams, stationary-phase spectra, windowed first-order coherence functions, and quantum-noise stability maps for strongly chirped dissipative solitons of the cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in normal and anomalous group-delay dispersion regimes. The repository includes node-regularized normal-dispersion spectra and energies; small-parameter expansions of the branch roots; cavity-map gain-loss update relations; Airy uniformization at the normal-dispersion spectral edge; anomalous-dispersion spectra and coherence calculations; and processed tables for plotting and stability analysis. OriginLab projects are accompanied by open-format .csv/.txt numerical tables to support reuse without proprietary plotting software. Data and code repository: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22690899.
summary: This work delivers a comprehensive data package and theoretical framework for studying strongly chirped dissipative solitons governed by the cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equation. It details methods to calculate spectral properties and map out the stability boundaries under quantum noise in both normal and anomalous dispersion regimes. The resource is valuable for researchers needing to benchmark numerical simulations in nonlinear wave physics.
main_problem: The paper provides comprehensive datasets and analytical tools to reproduce complex spectral and stability analyses for strongly chirped dissipative solitons.
main_result: The analysis characterizes the existence, spectral properties, and quantum-noise stability regions of these solitons across normal and anomalous dispersion regimes.
method: The study employs adiabatic theory, stationary-phase approximations, uniformization techniques, and stochastic propagation simulations to analyze the nonlinear evolution.
model_or_system: The system is governed by the cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation (CGLE), modeling dissipative solitons in nonlinear wave propagation.
key_observables: Stationary-phase spectra, windowed first-order coherence functions, quantum-noise stability maps, and energy ($	ext{ENGD}(	ilde{\chi})$).
important_parameters: Dispersion regimes (Normal/Anomalous), normalized control parameters ($\Sigma, \delta C$), and the chirp parameter ($	ilde{\chi}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the adiabatic approximation (large-chirp limit) and the use of finite-time stochastic classification for stability.
figures_summary: Figure 1 maps stability regions in parameter space under quantum noise; Figure 2 compares the analytical soliton profile against its noisy, perturbed realization.
paper_structure: The structure moves from defining the CGLE and its parameters, through deriving analytical approximations for energy and spectral features (SPA, uniformization), to analyzing the stability via stochastic simulation and presenting the final data repository.
why_interesting: The detailed mathematical machinery, involving spectral analysis and stability mapping under noise, is highly relevant to open quantum systems and nonlinear wave dynamics, bridging quantum optics and nonlinear PDEs.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Stability regions of the analytical strongly chirped AGD-DS under quantum-noise perturbations. The stability criterion is P_ surv >50%, where P_ surv is the fraction of noisy realizations that remain single-pulse, do not reach the perturbation cutoff ∥δa∥/∥a_0∥=0.25, and retain high spectral correlation with the analytical reference over the propagation interval. Yellow denotes the stable/long-lived region, and blue denotes unstable points. The vertical dashed line marks the AGD-- DSR condition δC =0, where C =-1 /~χ +δC. Parameters common to both panels are ~χ =1.5, κ / γ =0.1, ζ / γ =0.39, and α =Cβκ / γ (see Eqs. (1,2)). (a): Stability map in the ~E ,δC plane at fixed Σ=0.14....

Figure 2. DS power envelope (upper-left) and spectral profile (upper-right) for analytical solution (solid blue) and noisy perturbed one (dashed red). The bottom-left histogram demonstrates the spectral correlation of the shots with high Psurv from 64 independent noise realizations. The bottom-right histogram demonstrates the corresponding dimensionless energy distribution. The dimensionless energy equals ~E=8, C =-0.67, δC =-0.01, Σ=0.14, ~χ =1.5. Other parameters correspond to Figure 1.
